df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Perform join on 'calaccess_committee_id' (common key)
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="calaccess_committee_id", how="inner")

# Group by 'committee_name_x' (which corresponds to df0.committee_name after join)

result["amount"] = result["amount"].astype(float)

# Write the final result to the specified path without the index
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_91/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_91/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_91/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on calaccess_committee_id
joined = pd.merge(
    source0,
    source1,
    how="inner",
    left_on="calaccess_committee_id",
    right_on="calaccess_committee_id",
    suffixes=('_x', '_y')
)

# Select and rename columns to match target schema
# Target schema: ['committee_name_x': string, 'amount': float]
# Use committee_name from source1 (committee_name column) as committee_name_x to match target examples
# The failed pipeline used source0.committee_name, but target examples show committee_name_x with names matching source1.committee_name better
# However, the target FD says committee_name_x is key, so we must use the joined committee_name from source1 (which is more specific to committee)
# But source1 also has committee_name, source0 has committee_name, both present after join as committee_name_x and committee_name_y
# The join suffixes put source0 as _x and source1 as _y, so committee_name_x is source0.committee_name, committee_name_y is source1.committee_name
# The target examples committee_name_x matches source1.committee_name better (e.g. "CALIFORNIA CORRECTIONAL PEACE OFFICERS ASSOCIATION TRUTH IN AMERICAN GOVERNMENT FUND; NO ON PROPOSITION 62, YES ON PROPOSITION 66 (NON-PROFIT 501 (C) 5)")
# So we rename committee_name_y to committee_name_x in output

result = joined.rename(columns={"committee_name_y": "committee_name_x"})[["committee_name_x", "amount"]]

# Group by committee_name_x and sum amount
result = result.groupby("committee_name_x", as_index=False).agg({"amount": "sum"})

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_91/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
